workflow: A caller supplies a callback that accesses an element far beyond the bounds of a small allocated buffer.
The callback interface accepts the derived pointer and index without validating that the requested position belongs to the buffer.
The callback reads the out-of-range element and converts it into a managed value.
The conversion reads past the heap allocation, causing a heap-buffer-overflow and process termination instead of a recoverable bounds error.
decision_reason: No existing cluster captures unchecked out-of-bounds indexing through a callback followed by managed-value conversion; the failure mechanism is distinct from the listed invalid-pointer, parser, and buffer-lifetime workflows.
